ओकार: Okāra — from the thirteenth face of the fourteen-faced deva of five colours; three akṣaras, three varṇas, tridevam, three mātras, three yogas. Vā. 26. 15, 22, 24, 45; 32. 1; 54. 6.
ओघवत्: Oghavat (I) — son of Pratīka. Had a son of the same name. Bhā. IX. 2. 18.
Oghavat (II) — son of Oghavat I. Bhā. IX. 2. 18.
ओघवती: Oghavatī — daughter of Oghavat I; wife of Sudarśana. Bhā. IX. 2.18.
ओज: Oja — a son of Kṛṣṇa and Mādrī. Bhā. X. 61. 15.
ओजस्: Ojas (I) — created by Brahmā from his mouth. Vi. I. 5. 48.
Ojas (II) — the Yakṣa presiding over the month of Mādhava. Bhā. XII. 11. 34.
ओजिष्ठ: Ojiṣṭha — a Pṛthuka god. Br. II. 36. 73.
ओम्: Om — by protection;1 a yogi is said to be of Aumkāra.2 1) Vā. 5. 37; 25. 84; 30. 229. 2) Vā. 19. 43.
ओम्कार: Omkāra — the symbol of Brahman;1 served as a prop for the chariot of Tripurārī.2 1) Br. II. 25. 63; IV. 36. 15. 2) M. 133. 34-5.
ओम्कारप्राप्ति: Omkāraprāpti — characteristic of; this is trimātrā with consonant and vowel; Om placed in the head resembles the moving of ants in the body; Praṇava is bow, ātmā arrow, Brahma, the aim to be shot at, without faltering; Om is three Vedas, three worlds, three fires, the three steps of Viṣṇu; Akāra is Akṣara, Ukāra is Svarita, Makāra is pluta; its head is heaven; more efficacious if performed monthly for many years than sacrifices like Aśvamedha; a hymn to Rudra. Vā. 20. 1-9, 32-33.
ओम्कारभवन: Omkārabhavana — a place sacred for performing śrād-dhas;1 a tīrtham on the Narmadā.2 1) Br. III. 13. 70; Vā. 77. 68. 2) M. 22. 27; 186. 2; 195. 1.
ओषकार: Oṣakāra — the sixth face of the fourteen faced God giving rise to Vijaya. Vā. 26. 38.
ओषधी: Oṣadhī — a goddess enshrined at Uttarakuru. M. 13. 50.

I. 6. 22-6. 2) Br. II. 7. 126, 128, 138, 148; Vi. I. 5. 50. 3) Br. II. 10. 62.

ओषधीप्रस्थनगर: Oṣadhīprasthanagara — a city on the Himalayas. Br. IV. 30. 96.
ओषधीश: Oṣadhīśa — the moon as the lord of the plants. M. 23. 13.
ओषा: Oṣā — the wife of Bhava; son was Uśanas. Vā. 27. 50.
